title: Español para padres
about: Ten lessons for grown-ups on Spanish family life: chatting at the school gate, the parent-teacher meeting, the class WhatsApp group, school forms, the health centre, the chemist's, pick-up, neighbours, party invitations and the town hall.

lessons.title: En la puerta del cole
lessons.subtitle: Hello at the school gate
lessons.funFact: At the gate, Spanish parents greet each other with a quick '¡Hola! ¿Qué tal?', and often two kisses (dos besos) once they know you. A handshake is fine at first.

phrase.es: Hola, soy la madre de Mia. Somos nuevos.
phrase.en: Hi, I'm Mia's mum. We're new.

sentences.en: I'm Leo's dad.
My daughter is in Year 3.

opts: See you on the way in

story.title: New at the Gate
paras: Emma has just moved to Spain with her daughter Mia. On the first morning, another mum smiles at her at the school gate.
'Hola, soy la madre de Mia. Somos nuevos,' says Emma. 'Encantada. Yo soy Carmen, la madre de Lucía. ¿En qué clase está Mia?'
'Está en primero.' 'Como Lucía. ¡Nos vemos a la salida!'

qs.q: When will they see each other again?

lessons.title: La tutoría
lessons.subtitle: Meeting the class teacher
lessons.funFact: Each class in Spain has a 'tutor' or 'tutora', the class teacher. A 'tutoría' is a one-to-one meeting with them, usually booked through the agenda or the school app.

phrase.en: How is Mia getting on in class?

words.en: How's he/she getting on in class?
How can we help at home?

sentences.en: He/she finds reading a bit hard.
How can we help at home?

story.title: The First Meeting
paras: Emma has a tutoría with Mia's teacher, Ana. 'Buenas tardes. ¿Qué tal va Mia en clase?'
'Muy bien. Se porta bien y está muy contenta. Le cuesta un poco la lectura en español, pero es normal.'
'¿Cómo podemos ayudar en casa?' 'Leed un cuento juntos cada noche.' Emma smiles: that's easy!

qs.q: What does Mia find a bit hard?

opts: Reading a story together every night

lessons.title: El grupo de WhatsApp
lessons.subtitle: The class parents' group
lessons.funFact: Almost every class in Spain has a parents' WhatsApp group. It's where you find out about trips, birthdays, costumes and forgotten jumpers. A short '¡Gracias!' is always welcome.

phrase.en: Does anyone know if there's a trip tomorrow?

words.en: What do we need to bring?
Thanks a lot for letting us know

sentences.en: What do we need to bring on the trip?
Thanks a lot for letting us know.

story.title: Ping! Ping! Ping!
paras: Emma's phone goes ping twenty times. It's the class WhatsApp group. Someone writes: 'Mañana es la excursión al zoo.'
Emma types slowly: '¿Qué hay que llevar?' Carmen answers: 'La merienda, agua y gorra.'
Emma replies: '¡Muchas gracias por avisar!' Three parents send a thumbs-up.

qs.q: What do they need to bring?
opts: A snack, water and a cap

lessons.title: Papeles del cole
lessons.subtitle: School forms and notes
lessons.funFact: Spanish schools send home lots of paper: 'autorizaciones' (permission slips) for trips, forms for the 'comedor' (school lunch) and 'actividades extraescolares' (after-school clubs). Most need a signature: 'firma del padre, madre o tutor legal'.

phrase.en: I have to sign the permission slip.

sentences.en: I have to sign the permission slip.
The deadline is Friday.

story.title: The Pile of Paper
paras: Mia comes home with three papers in her mochila. Emma reads the first: 'Autorización para la excursión.' She signs it.
The second is for the comedor next month. The third is about extraescolares: football or music?
'¿Hasta cuándo?' asks Emma. Mia points to the bottom: 'El plazo termina el viernes, mamá.'

qs.q: How many papers does Mia bring home?

opts: A permission slip for a trip

lessons.title: En el centro de salud
lessons.subtitle: At the health centre
lessons.funFact: In Spain your family doctor and the children's 'pediatra' are at your local 'centro de salud'. Bring the 'tarjeta sanitaria' (health card) and ask for 'cita' (an appointment), often online or by app.

phrase.es: Quería pedir cita con la pediatra.
phrase.en: I'd like to make an appointment with the paediatrician.

sentences.en: My son has had a temperature since yesterday.
I'd like to make an appointment with the paediatrician.

story.title: A Hot Forehead
paras: Leo wakes up hot and grumpy. His dad, Tom, phones the centro de salud. 'Quería pedir cita con la pediatra. Mi hijo tiene fiebre desde ayer.'
'¿Tiene la tarjeta sanitaria?' 'Sí.' 'Vale, a las once.'
The pediatra listens to Leo's chest. 'Es un virus. Mucha agua y descanso.' No receta needed.

opts: It's a virus: lots of water and rest

lessons.title: En la farmacia
lessons.subtitle: At the chemist's
lessons.funFact: Spanish pharmacists give a lot of friendly advice, so the 'farmacia' (look for the green cross) is often the first stop for small problems. At night and at weekends, a 'farmacia de guardia' (duty pharmacy) is open.

phrase.en: Have you got anything for a cough?

sentences.en: Have you got anything for a cough?
It's for my six-year-old daughter.

story.title: The Green Cross
paras: Mia has a cough at night. In the morning, Emma looks for the green cross. 'Buenos días. ¿Tiene algo para la tos? Es para mi hija de seis años.'
The pharmacist gives her a jarabe para niños. '¿Cada cuántas horas?' 'Cada ocho horas, con la comida.'
'¿Y tiene tiritas de dibujos?' Mia will be happy: they've got unicorns on them!

qs.q: How often should Mia take it?

lessons.title: La recogida
lessons.subtitle: Pick-up and after school
lessons.funFact: Many Spanish schools have a 'jornada continua' (school ends around 2pm) or a 'jornada partida' (with a long lunch break). If someone else is collecting your child, tell the school first.

phrase.en: His grandmother is picking him up today.

words.en: His grandma is picking him up today
The school day without a lunch break

sentences.en: His grandmother is picking him up today.
I'm running ten minutes late.

story.title: Stuck in Traffic
paras: Tom is stuck in traffic. He calls the school. 'Hola, soy el padre de Leo. Llego tarde diez minutos.'
'No pasa nada. Leo puede esperar en conserjería.' Tom feels better.
Tomorrow his mother is visiting, so he adds: 'Y mañana lo recoge su abuela.' 'Vale, lo apunto.'

lessons.title: Los vecinos
lessons.subtitle: Meeting the neighbours
lessons.funFact: Most people in Spanish towns live in flats, and the 'comunidad de vecinos' (residents' association) holds a 'junta' (meeting) once or twice a year. Saying hello in the lift goes a long way.

phrase.es: Hola, somos los nuevos del tercero.
phrase.en: Hi, we're the new people on the third floor.

words.en: We're the new people on the third floor
If you need anything, we're here

sentences.en: We're the new people on the third floor.
Sorry about the children's noise.

opts: If you need anything, we're here

story.title: In the Lift
paras: In the lift, Emma meets an older woman. 'Hola, somos los nuevos del tercero.' 'Ah, encantada. Yo soy Pilar, del quinto.'
Emma adds: 'Perdón por el ruido de los niños.' Pilar laughs. 'Tranquila, me encantan los niños.'
At the door, Pilar says: 'Cualquier cosa, aquí estamos.' A week later, she brings a plate of rosquillas.

lessons.title: ¡Un cumpleaños!
lessons.subtitle: Birthday party invitations
lessons.funFact: Children's birthday parties in Spain often happen at a 'parque de bolas' (soft play) or in the park, and sometimes the whole class is invited. Parents often club together for one shared present, organised in the WhatsApp group.

phrase.en: Can Mia come to the birthday party?

sentences.en: Thank you very much for the invitation.
What time does the party finish?

opts: Shall we put it in a jar?

story.title: Lucía's Party
paras: Mia brings home an invitation: Lucía's birthday is on Saturday at the parque de bolas.
In the WhatsApp group, Carmen writes: '¿Ponemos un bote para el regalo? Cinco euros cada uno.' Emma answers: '¡Genial!'
Then she writes: 'Muchas gracias por la invitación. ¿A qué hora termina?' 'A las siete.' '¡Allí estaremos!'

qs.q: How much does each family put in?
What time does the party finish?

lessons.title: En el ayuntamiento
lessons.subtitle: At the town hall
lessons.funFact: When you move to a Spanish town, you sign up on the 'padrón' (local register) at the 'ayuntamiento' (town hall). You need it for school places and the health centre. Most offices ask for 'cita previa', an appointment booked in advance.

phrase.en: I've come to register on the padrón.

sentences.en: Which documents do I need for the padrón?
I have an appointment at ten.

story.title: The Padrón
paras: Tom and Emma go to the ayuntamiento. 'Buenos días. Tenemos cita previa a las diez. Venimos a empadronarnos.'
'¿Tienen los pasaportes y el contrato de alquiler?' 'Sí, aquí están.' 'Y una fotocopia, por favor.'
Twenty minutes later they have their certificado: they are on the padrón. Now they can sign up at the centro de salud!

qs.q: What do they need to bring?

opts: Sign up at the health centre

turns.askEn: Hi! I don't know you. Are you new?
turns.answer: Sí, somos nuevos. Soy la madre de Mia.
turns.answerEn: Yes, we're new. I'm Mia's mum.
also: Sí, somos nuevos. Soy el padre de Leo.

turns.askEn: Which class is she in?
turns.answerEn: She's in Year 1.

turns.ask: Yo soy Carmen, la madre de Lucía.
turns.askEn: I'm Carmen, Lucía's mum.
turns.answerEn: Nice to meet you, Carmen.

turns.ask: Buenas tardes. Siéntese, por favor. ¿Qué quería saber?
turns.askEn: Good afternoon. Please sit down. What did you want to know?
turns.answerEn: How's Mia getting on in class?
turns.reply: Va muy bien. Está muy contenta.
turns.replyEn: She's doing very well. She's very happy.

turns.askEn: Is there anything that worries you?
turns.answer: Le cuesta un poco la lectura.
turns.answerEn: She finds reading a bit hard.

turns.askEn: Do you have any other questions?
turns.answerEn: How can we help at home?
turns.reply: Leed un cuento juntos cada noche.
turns.replyEn: Read a story together every night.

turns.ask: Mañana es la excursión al zoo. ¿Tienes alguna pregunta?
turns.askEn: Tomorrow is the trip to the zoo. Do you have any questions?
turns.answerEn: What do we need to bring?
turns.reply: La merienda, agua y una gorra.
turns.replyEn: A snack, water and a cap.

turns.ask: ¡Ah! Y el viernes es fiesta. Mañana no, ¡el viernes!
turns.askEn: Oh! And Friday is a holiday. Not tomorrow, Friday!
turns.answerEn: Thanks a lot for letting us know.

turns.ask: Leo se ha dejado la chaqueta en clase. ¿Alguien la tiene?
turns.askEn: Leo has left his jacket in class. Has anyone got it?
turns.answerEn: No, sorry.
turns.replyEn: OK, I'll ask the class teacher.

turns.ask: Hay que devolver la autorización para la excursión. ¿La tienes?
turns.askEn: You need to return the permission slip for the trip. Have you got it?
turns.answer: Sí, tengo que firmar la autorización.
turns.answerEn: Yes, I have to sign the permission slip.

turns.askEn: Is Mia staying for school lunch?
turns.answerEn: Yes, she's staying for lunch.
turns.replyEn: Very good, I'll write it down.

turns.ask: Las inscripciones de extraescolares ya están abiertas.
turns.askEn: Sign-ups for after-school clubs are now open.
turns.answerEn: When's the deadline?

turns.ask: Centro de salud, buenos días. ¿Qué desea?
turns.askEn: Health centre, good morning. How can I help?
turns.answer: Quería pedir cita con la pediatra.
turns.answerEn: I'd like an appointment with the paediatrician.
turns.reply: Muy bien. ¿Qué le pasa al niño?
turns.replyEn: Fine. What's wrong with the child?

turns.askEn: What's wrong?
turns.answerEn: He's had a temperature since yesterday.
turns.reply: Vale, puede venir a las once.
turns.replyEn: OK, you can come at eleven.

turns.askEn: Have you got the child's health card?
turns.answerEn: Yes, I've got it here.

turns.askEn: Good morning. What do you need?
turns.answerEn: Have you got anything for a cough?

turns.ask: ¿Es para usted o para un niño?
turns.askEn: Is it for you or for a child?
turns.answer: Es para mi hija de seis años.
turns.answerEn: It's for my six-year-old daughter.

turns.askEn: Here's the syrup.
turns.answerEn: How often should she take it?
turns.reply: Cada ocho horas, con la comida.

turns.askEn: School, hello?
turns.answer: Hola, soy el padre de Leo. Llego tarde.
turns.answerEn: Hi, I'm Leo's dad. I'm running late.
also: Hola, soy la madre de Mia. Llego tarde.
turns.replyEn: No problem. How long will you be?

turns.askEn: How long are you going to be?
turns.answerEn: I'm ten minutes late.
turns.reply: Vale, Leo puede esperar en conserjería.
turns.replyEn: OK, Leo can wait at the office.

turns.askEn: Are you collecting him tomorrow?
turns.answer: No, mañana lo recoge su abuela.
turns.answerEn: No, his grandmother is collecting him tomorrow.

turns.askEn: Hi! You're not from here, are you?
turns.answerEn: We're the new people on the third floor.
turns.replyEn: Ah, nice to meet you! I'm on the fifth floor.

turns.askEn: How's the flat?
turns.answer: Muy bien, pero perdón por el ruido.
turns.answerEn: Very good, but sorry about the noise.
turns.replyEn: Don't worry, you can't hear a thing.

turns.askEn: If you need anything, we're here.
turns.answerEn: Thank you very much, very kind.

turns.ask: El sábado es el cumpleaños de Lucía en el parque de bolas. ¿Puede venir Mia?
turns.askEn: Saturday is Lucía's birthday at soft play. Can Mia come?
turns.answerEn: Yes! Thank you very much for the invitation.
turns.reply: ¡Qué bien! Lucía se va a alegrar mucho.
turns.replyEn: Great! Lucía will be really pleased.

turns.askEn: It starts at five.
turns.answerEn: What time does it finish?

turns.ask: Para el regalo, ¿ponemos un bote entre todos?
turns.askEn: For the present, shall we all chip in?
turns.answerEn: Yes, of course! How much shall we put in?

turns.askEn: Good morning. Do you have an appointment?
turns.answer: Sí, tengo cita previa a las diez.
turns.answerEn: Yes, I have an appointment at ten.
turns.reply: Muy bien. ¿Qué trámite viene a hacer?
turns.replyEn: Very good. What have you come to do?

turns.askEn: What have you come to do?
turns.answerEn: I've come to register on the padrón.

turns.ask: ¿Tiene el pasaporte y el contrato de alquiler?
turns.askEn: Have you got your passport and rental contract?
turns.answerEn: Yes, here they are.
turns.replyEn: Perfect. I also need a photocopy.

turns.ask: Ya está. Aquí tiene el certificado.
turns.askEn: Done. Here's the certificate.
turns.answerEn: Thank you very much. Goodbye!
